name: Immersive Labeling Primitives
summary: In VR, a sphere, cube or clipping plane attached to the controller labels or deletes every point inside it when the trigger is pressed, with instant visual feedback even in very large point clouds.
howItWorks: Sphere and cube primitives are for painting labels on nearby points; their size is set with the left touchpad. The clipping plane cuts large sets of points off a wall or boundary at once. A chunk-based CPU/GPU data structure keeps rendering at high frame rates while labels change. Users move by teleporting, grabbing and scaling the cloud, or stepping along the controller. In a study with 25 participants on three room-scale scenes, labelling was faster than with Pointly.AI on a desktop and with Shooting Labels in VR, especially with heavy occlusion.
advantages: Fast labelling with immediate feedback in large clouds.
Handled heavy occlusion better than the compared tools.
limitations: Results come from a two-page abstract with limited detail.

relationships.note: Both paint a selection with a sphere attached to the hand.
